title: Sanitation in urban India
body:
Read the extract from the article 'A new deal for old cities' (summarised) and answer the question.

In the absence of a hygienic environment and safe water supply, chronic water-borne diseases such as cholera continue to stalk the poor in the biggest cities. As per the Census of India 2001, nearly 14 million Indian households in urban areas (26 per cent of the total) do not have a latrine within the house, and some 14 per cent have only rudimentary 'pit' facilities. The number of households without a drainage connection stands at 11.8 million (22.1 per cent). Migration to cities continues, and infrastructure to treat sewage is grossly inadequate to meet the demand even where it exists. The writer argues that the quality of the urban environment is unlikely to be dramatically improved if such fundamental questions remain unresolved.
